summary: Gov. Joe Lombardo (Republican) ran for re-election and lost to Aaron Ford (Democrat), the state attorney general.

candidates.name: Aaron Ford
candidates.bio: Aaron Ford has been Nevada Attorney General since 2019. He is a former state Senate majority leader and former math teacher.

positions.summary: Says he would repeal Nevada's right-to-work law, cap how many homes corporate investors can buy each year, and cap security deposits at one month's rent.
Says he would cap many prescription drug prices at the Medicare-negotiated rate, protect Medicaid, and relieve medical debt for eligible Nevadans.
Says he would raise per-pupil funding to meet or exceed the national average and guarantee school breakfast and lunch to all Nevada children.
Says he would stop NV Energy's residential demand charge, prioritize clean energy development, and require data centers to pay for their own energy and grid upgrades.
Supports enshrining abortion rights through 24 weeks in the state constitution.

candidates.name: Joe Lombardo
candidates.bio: Joe Lombardo is a Republican and a former Clark County sheriff who has been Nevada's governor since 2023. He ran for re-election in 2026.

positions.summary: Touts raises for teachers, including charter school teachers, and has pushed to expand school choice.
Asked the White House not to cut Medicaid funding to Nevada.
Allowed the Nevada National Guard to help with federal immigration enforcement for a time, in a logistics role.
Personally supports a 15-week cutoff but says abortion rights are codified in state law and should be left to voters.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called)
